_comment: The documentation the assistant is allowed to read, and nothing else.
This file is an allowlist on purpose. Left to crawl freely, discovery
reached a 13,186-word generated market list and a 12,506-word type
reference -- pages nobody asks about, whose vocabulary competes with the
pages they do. docs.sportradar.com is the sharper warning: its llms.txt
indexes 2,999 pages, of which 6 are Engagement Tools.
`products` is also the entity tagging. A passage is about whatever this
file says its section is about, because a page's own URL is a better
signal than anything mined out of prose -- both regressions in the thread
ingest were tagging failures. Use exact catalogue labels: the entity veto
compares lowercased label strings, so a near-miss silently turns a 1.6x
`slugPrefix` narrows a section when the folder holds unrelated pages.
/widgets/docs/widgets/match/ is the Player Prop Zone section AND the home
of sixteen unrelated statistics widgets, so the prefix keeps the tag off

apidocs.sportradar.com.why: No llms.txt (404) and appending .md returns the app shell as HTML -- a soft 200 with zero headings. The sidebar is client-rendered, so discovery needs a real browser; the rendered <main> was verified to contain every content heading.

docs.sportradar.com.why: GitBook. Every page serves text/markdown at .md. Its root llms.txt is curated rather than complete (it omits bet-utility-api, which the catalogue links), and no per-section llms.txt exists, so pages are listed explicitly below.

developer.sportradar.com.why: ReadMe. Serves text/markdown at .md with updatedAt frontmatter, and /getting-started/docs/llms.txt is a complete section index.

_skipWhy./tutorials/references/: generated attribute and market dumps, 13,186 words on one page
_skipWhy.@sportradar.com: the crawler found /tutorials/sales@sportradar.com, a page invented by a mailto link

_caps.maxDepth: path segments allowed below a section prefix; default 3. Virtual Stadium is 2 because its section is an entire separate documentation site.
_caps.declaredVsDiscovered: A declared URL that fails is a build failure. A link merely discovered on their pages that 404s is their broken link -- reported, never fatal. 45 broken virtual-stadium links would otherwise block every run.
